facts.statement: The study addresses radiation-induced brain injury, a serious side effect occurring in up to 30% of patients who receive radiation to the head.
facts.subject: humans

facts.statement: Researchers tested a new nanomaterial on mice that had received a specific dose of whole-body radiation to see if it could fix brain function.
facts.subject: animals

facts.statement: The mice were given a dose of radiation equal to 6 grays before receiving the treatment.
facts.subject: animals

facts.statement: The scientists used electrical recordings inside living animals to measure how the treatment changed brain cell activity.
facts.subject: animals

facts.statement: The treatment helped restore the electrical activity of specific brain cells and improved the animals' movement and anxiety levels.
facts.subject: animals

facts.statement: The treatment also protected other organs and helped blood cell recovery, allowing all treated mice to survive for 30 days.
facts.subject: animals

facts.statement: The authors suggest that fixing how neurons fire electrically is a new and promising way to treat radiation brain injury.
facts.subject: animals
